issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of the record page only shows `person1 == person2` staying True when both records share one array. It does not state that the synthesized Equals uses `EqualityComparer<TField>.Default`. The second link (the EqualityComparer<T>.Default page) does not show that arrays use reference equality or that records use this comparer. The mechanism comes from the C# records proposal, and neither excerpt backs it.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the C# record/records proposal or spec page as a link (kind spec) and cite it for the field-comparer claim. Or reword to 'compares each field using that field type's equality; arrays do not override Equals, so the references are compared'. Keep the record page as the source for 'records get value equality'. Apply the same change in ru.

issues.claim: declare your own `Equals(Order other)` in the record using `SequenceEqual`
issues.problem: For a non-sealed record the user-declared method must be `public virtual bool Equals(Order? other)`. The bare signature without modifiers may mislead. Hand-written `Equals` does not compile with a shorter signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Write 'declare your own `public virtual bool Equals(Order? other)` that compares `Items` with `SequenceEqual`, and a matching `GetHashCode`'. Make the same change in ru.

issues.problem: The hint nearly states the reason. The ru and en hints match each other, but the hint is stronger than a nudge.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften it to: 'Как сгенерированный Equals сравнивает поле типа int[] - по содержимому или иначе?' Make the same change in en.

issues.claim: the documentation states that a delegate with a return value returns the result of the last method invoked
issues.problem: Neither fetched excerpt contains this statement. 'Using delegates' says only 'The delegate returns the return value, if any, from the method'. The 'How to combine delegates' page uses void delegates and says nothing about return values. The claim is attributed to documentation the excerpts do not show.
issues.suggestedFix: Cite the C# language specification on delegate invocation, which says the return value comes from the last delegate in the list: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/language-specification/delegates (kind spec). Or reword to 'a multicast call has a single return value, which comes from the last delegate in the invocation list'. Make the same change in ru ('документация говорит').
